findings.issue_text: [Medium/performance] calendar-cache.repository.ts:173 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` filters only on `credentialId`, but `CalendarCache` has no index leading with that column (its composite unique is `[key, credentialId, userId]`), so the `groupBy` scans a high-volume table and runs on every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query; no supporting index is added in the migration — add `@@index([credentialId])` (plus migration) or query via the existing key-based unique index.

[Medium/performance] CalendarService.ts:1024 — the new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(...)` executes an UPDATE over all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential on the availability hot path (hit by every booking-page availability check), adding a write query and row-lock contention to a read flow that previously had none; only do this when a fresh fetch actually occurred, or fold it into the existing cache write.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests are added anywhere in the diff: `deleteCache.handler.ts` (especially the ownership check), `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, `updateManyByCredentialId`, the `connectedCalendars` enrichment, and `CredentialActionsDropdown`'s `hasCache`/`canDisconnect` rendering logic are all untested, even though the repository mock was updated — suggesting test infrastructure exists to cover them.

[Low/api] deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — throws a plain `Error` instead of `TRPCError` for the expected "not found / not owned" case, which surfaces as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; use `TRPCError` with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN (repo convention) so clients get a meaningful code.

[Low/api] deleteCache.handler.ts:28 and connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 — both bypass the `CalendarCacheRepository` abstraction: one handler re-implements `deleteManyByCredential` with raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` (duplicating the deletion logic and ignoring the mock/"calendar-cache disabled" behavior), while the other instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly; route both through the repository so the code path stays consistent when the feature is disabled.

[Low/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:96 — `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` hardcodes the locale; the app is fully localized and `useLocale()` already provides the active language, so non-English users will see US-formatted dates/times (12-hour, MM/DD) in the cache status.

[Low/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:86 — the icon-only trigger button (`variant="icon" StartIcon="ellipsis"`) has no accessible name (no `aria-label`), so screen readers announce an unnamed "button".

[Medium/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:91-119 — the action `DropdownItem`s are `<button>`s nested inside `DropdownMenuItem`s (`role="menuitem"`): nested interactive controls are invalid ARIA, and keyboard activation (Enter/Space) fires on the menu item rather than the inner button, so "Delete cached data"/"Remove app" are likely not operable by keyboard — a regression vs. the previous standalone `DisconnectIntegration` button; attach handlers to the `DropdownMenuItem` itself instead of nesting buttons.

[Low/bug] SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:70,123 — the `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` container is now always rendered even when `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns null (non-Google apps or delegated credentials without cache), leaving an empty 8rem div where nothing was rendered before — a layout regression; move the width into the component or conditionally render the wrapper.

[Low/data] migration.sql:9 (add_calendar_cache_updated_at) — existing `CalendarCache` rows are all stamped `updatedAt = NOW()` at migration time, so the new "Last updated" UI immediately shows the migration timestamp for caches that are actually old/stale; consider backfilling a more truthful value (e.g., derived from `expiresAt`) or explicitly accepting the inaccuracy for legacy rows.

[Low/bug] test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 — `sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; on GNU sed (Linux/CI/containers) the empty argument is treated as the script and the substitution as a filename, so the in-place update fails; use portable in-place editing or branch on OS.

[Low/data] CalendarService.ts:1024 / user.ts:899 / getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21 — the value written by the new availability-path touch is not consumed by this feature (the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`), and the newly selected `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` fields added to the user query/types are unused in this diff; additionally, `updateManyByCredentialId(id, {})` relies on Prisma implicitly applying `@updatedAt` for an empty `data` object — pass `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly and clarify where this timestamp is meant to be read.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] calendar-cache.repository.ts:173 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` filters only on `credentialId`, but `CalendarCache` has no index leading with that column (its composite unique is `[key, credentialId, userId]`), so the `groupBy` scans a high-volume table and runs on every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query; no supporting index is added in the migration — add `@@index([credentialId])` (plus migration) or query via the existing key-based unique index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` which runs a `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ by: ["credentialId"], where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds }}, _max: { updatedAt: true } })` and `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now calls it on every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` request to enrich each connected calendar with `cacheUpdatedAt`. That creates a potentially expensive query path on a likely high-volume table. However, the claim that there is definitively no supporting index (and that the only relevant index is a composite unique `[key, credentialId, userId]`) is not verifiable from the shown schema diff because the model-level indexes/uniques for `CalendarCache` are not included in this hunk. So the performance concern is real and diff-grounded, but the specific “no index exists” assertion can’t be confirmed from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional write query in `CalendarService.ts` right after the availability/cache logic: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});`. Because it’s outside the `if` block that fetches and caches availability, it will run on every invocation of that method, even when no fresh fetch occurred (e.g., cache hit). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern (extra DB write / potential contention in what appears to be an availability flow), though the claim about “every booking-page availability check” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:91-119 — the action `DropdownItem`s are `<button>`s nested inside `DropdownMenuItem`s (`role="menuitem"`): nested interactive controls are invalid ARIA, and keyboard activation (Enter/Space) fires on the menu item rather than the inner button, so "Delete cached data"/"Remove app" are likely not operable by keyboard — a regression vs. the previous standalone `DisconnectIntegration` button; attach handlers to the `DropdownMenuItem` itself instead of nesting buttons.

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the actionable entries are structured as <DropdownMenuItem> wrappers containing <DropdownItem type="button" ... onClick=...>. This is a nested interactive pattern (menu item + inner button) and the click/activation handler is attached to the inner button, not the menu item itself. If DropdownMenuItem behaves like a real menuitem (common in dropdown/menu primitives), keyboard activation (Enter/Space) would activate/select the menu item rather than firing the inner button’s onClick, making “Delete cached data”/“Remove app” potentially inaccessible/broken for keyboard users.

adjudication.rationale: In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx, the `actions` prop now always renders `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` wrapping `CredentialActionsDropdown` (both occurrences in the diff). `CredentialActionsDropdown` can return `null` when `!canDisconnect && !hasCache` (e.g., delegated credential + no cache, or non-Google with disconnect disabled), leaving an empty fixed-width `w-32` container. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `updatedAt` column to `CalendarCache` with `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` in the migration (`migration.sql`) and `@default(now()) @updatedAt` in the Prisma schema. That means any pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows will be assigned the migration/deploy time as `updatedAt`, regardless of when the cache was actually written. The new UI reads and displays `cacheUpdatedAt` (from `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `_max.updatedAt`, then rendered as `cache_last_updated`), so legacy caches can appear “recently updated” immediately after migration. This is a diff-grounded data/UX correctness concern rather than a hard runtime defect.
